consideredAndDeclined.item: OBL-ID-DEP-12 is classified specified-not-leftover, though doctor v4's ID-DEP-12 records the authorization origin as riding NOTHING THAT EXISTS and UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED
consideredAndDeclined.analysis: This is the sharpest question in the artifact and I spent the most time on it. v4's ID-DEP-12 asks two things: whether host surfaces are subject to DR-105's vocabulary, and what governs host actors instead. D-032 answered the first by putting host-under-instruction outside DR-105. It did not mint the second; that origin is the host-effect contract, recorded as candidates at D-093 and D-126 and made live only by a joint-owner FC-C1 recording.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The live remainder is carried, not lost. OBL-FC-C1 is leftoverDesign true on this row and OBL-HE-V25 is recorded-candidate-not-applied, so the unmet authorization origin is classified as leftover under its own obligation. What OBL-ID-DEP-12 asserts is narrower and true: v4 named the mismatch unresolved in its frozen bytes, D-032 later decided the split, and this join neither rewrites v4 nor re-opens the actor question. Nothing is understated and DR-114 stays ineligible on ten leftover obligations regardless.

consideredAndDeclined.item: OBL-ID-DEP-12 was added without a findingDisposition entry, so three obligations appear where two dispositions are claimed
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The addition is scope-neutral — it lands in specifiedNotLeftover and leaves the leftover count driven only by the G21 harness specification — and it closes a gap I had independently noticed in v1, where ID-DEP-12 appeared only inside another obligation's reason. The findingDisposition block disposes findings; it does not claim to enumerate every edit. Charging an unannounced improvement that changes no classification would penalise the artifact for being more complete than it was asked to be.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Seventeen attacks run, none landed. First a disclosure: my v1 review was interrupted by a competing dispatch and never filed, so Codex's DALJ-V1-SF1 stands unopposed by me on the record. Worth knowing is that the check I was running at the time would not have found it — I was walking gate claims to test v1's assertion that no live gate owns actor-join fixture execution, and the G21 ride comes through a different route entirely, doctor v4's ID-DEP-11. Both dispositions land and I verified each in source rather than in the disposition block. G21's live owner cell reads Supervisor + protocol + operability, byte-exact with liveGateOwners and distinct from G12's owner; harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment appears verbatim in G21's live harness cell alongside not authored, which is what makes the specification leftover. v4's own ID-DEP-11 reads 'The acceptance harness that consumes the fixture classes', riding DR-G12 plus DR-G21 for the containment behaviour of a CA-1 probe's process tree — I checked v4's identityDependencies container specifically, because the string ID-DEP-11 also appears in v4 describing a different contract's dependency. FC-NC's consented variant requires exactly one supervised process, and v4's supervisionHonesty says that process tree is cancelled and reaped by the host, the containment behaviour DR-G21 covers. The advisory disposition names the D-127 and D-129 travelling honesty items. The change is additive: three obligations added, none removed, leftover growing by the G21 specification alone, both fixture sets still set-equal to their sources at twelve and thirteen, and a clean twenty-four-way partition. I tested whether the G21 addition quietly absorbs the actor-join execution question and it does not — that obligation is still leftover with its own reasoning, and G21's claim is component-failure containment, which is a different property. Two items are recorded as considered and declined. The sharper one is OBL-ID-DEP-12, classified specified-not-leftover although v4 records that dependency as riding nothing that exists and unowned-and-needed; I declined because the live remainder, the authorization origin that only a joint-owner FC-C1 recording supplies, is carried as its own leftover obligation, so nothing is understated and every sentence in the reason is true. The other is that OBL-ID-DEP-12 was added without a disposition entry, which is scope-neutral and closes a gap I had noticed in v1.
